description: Reopen r-sort-3-corpus-accdb (ACCDB) read-only. Reads (a.ID, b.ID) for every pair of T and of U rows where a.K = b.K and a.ID < b.ID (SQL self-join equality); (MIN ID, MAX ID, COUNT) for every K group with more than one row (GROUP BY K); COUNT of DISTINCT K in T; the IDs that survived the one-INSERT-per-row loads into the unique-indexed tables W (from T) and W2 (from U). Asks the public equality classes through SQL comparison, grouping and unique-index refusal, as separate observations.
retentionNote: Designed r-sort-3 probe (A-02); complete capture of the ACE answer.

question.description: Reopen r-sort-3-corpus-accdb (ACCDB) read-only. Reads (a.ID, b.ID) for every pair of T and of U rows where a.K = b.K and a.ID < b.ID (SQL self-join equality); (MIN ID, MAX ID, COUNT) for every K group with more than one row (GROUP BY K); COUNT of DISTINCT K in T; the IDs that survived the one-INSERT-per-row loads into the unique-indexed tables W (from T) and W2 (from U). Asks the public equality classes through SQL comparison, grouping and unique-index refusal, as separate observations.

args.text: SELECT a.ID, b.ID FROM T AS a, T AS b WHERE a.K = b.K AND a.ID < b.ID ORDER BY a.ID, b.ID
SELECT MIN(ID), MAX(ID), COUNT(*) FROM T GROUP BY K HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY MIN(ID)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT K FROM T)
SELECT a.ID, b.ID FROM U AS a, U AS b WHERE a.K = b.K AND a.ID < b.ID ORDER BY a.ID, b.ID
SELECT MIN(ID), MAX(ID), COUNT(*) FROM U GROUP BY K HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY MIN(ID)
SELECT ID FROM W ORDER BY ID
SELECT ID FROM W2 ORDER BY ID
